senses.gloss: भिक्षा- + अटन भिक्षा- + अटन, n. wandering about for begging alms, Pañc. 116, 17.

भिक्ष् भिक्ष् (for बिभक्ष्, desider. of भज्), i. 1, Ātm. (in epic poetry also Par., MBh. 3, 16986).
 1. To beg, Man. 2, 184.
 2. To solicit from, Man. 2, 50 (acc.); 11, 24 (abl.).
 3. † To obtain.
 4. † To fail of obtaining.
 5. † To be distressed.
 6. † To solicit anything through covetousness(?).

भिक्षा भिक्ष् + आ, f.
 1. Begging, [] Pañc. 116, 17.
 2. Alms., Pañc. 116, 19.
 3. Begged food, Man. 2, 50.
 4. Hire.
 5. Service.
 --Comp.
भिक्षाक भिक्षा + क, m., and f. की, A mendicant, Rājat. 6, 166.

भिक्षु भिक्ष् + उ, m.
 1. A mendicant; one who subsists only upon alms, Pañc. v. d. 55.
 2. A religious mendicant, Hit. iii. d. 104.
 --Comp.

भिक्षुक भिक्षु + क, m., and f. की, A beggar, Daśak. in Chr. 180, 14.
 --Comp.
